name: chmod
synopsis: int fchmodat(int dirfd, const char *pathname, mode_t mode, int flags);
description: The chmod(), fchmod(), and fchmodat() system calls change the mode bits of a file, including permissions and special flags like set-user-ID. They differ in how the file is specified: by pathname for chmod(), by file descriptor for fchmod(), and by directory file descriptor with optional flags for fchmodat().

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.description: Path to the file whose mode is to be changed

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Bit mask specifying the new file mode bits, including permissions and flags like S_ISUID

parameters.name: fd
parameters.description: File descriptor referring to the file whose mode is to be changed

parameters.name: dirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor or AT_FDCWD for relative paths

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags for fchmodat(), such as AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: Search permission is denied on a component of the path prefix
fd is not a valid file descriptor, or for fchmodat(), pathname is relative and dirfd is invalid
pathname points outside accessible address space
Invalid flag specified in flags for fchmodat()
Too many symbolic links encountered in resolving pathname
A component of the path prefix is not a directory, or for fchmodat(), pathname is relative and dirfd is not a directory
fchmodat() specified AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW, which is not supported
The effective UID does not match the owner, or the file is immutable/append-only
The file resides on a read-only filesystem

versions: chmod() and fchmod() from 4.4BSD, SVr4, POSIX.1-2001; fchmodat() from Linux 2.6.16 and glibc 2.4
